deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a pencil draft of a short personal letter by Riemann, with several crossed-out openings. It is written on the blank back of a printed 'Frachtkarte' (railway or freight waybill, form No. 2), which appears upside down at the foot of the page with the columns Inhalt, Auslage, Porto, Franko, 'abgegangen den ... 185.' and so on. Riemann reused it as scrap paper.

Content, after resolving the deletions and the successive reformulations:

(1) Lecture announcement. The addressee had asked Riemann, through Dr. Dedekind, for the announcement of his lectures for the next semester. Riemann would send it at once, but he hopes to ask the addressee's advice about it in person within the next few days. He tried three versions of this sentence; the final one begins 'Auf die Aufforderung, die Sie durch Hr. Dr. Dedekind an mich gütigst ergehen ließen, würde ich Ihnen die Ankündigung meiner Vorlesungen sofort einsenden, wenn ich nicht hoffte ...'.

(2) The Abelian paper. Riemann reports that today he sent his paper on the Abelian transcendental functions to Dr. Borchardt. A crossed-out word before 'Hr. Dr. Borchardt' may be 'Crelle'. Borchardt was editor of Crelle's Journal from 1856. Riemann adds that on returning to Göttingen he will ask permission to show the addressee a copy of the paper.

(3) Closing. Greetings to the addressee and his 'wertheste Frau Gemahlin', 'in dankbarster Gesinnung'. Dated 2 July 1857; the place name is uncertain. Signed 'Ihr ergebenster Schüler B. Riemann'.

Historical context:
- The paper is 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen', published in Crelle's Journal vol. 54 (1857).
- The addressee is most plausibly P. G. Lejeune Dirichlet. He was in Göttingen from 1855, and Riemann considered himself his pupil from Berlin. He was married to Rebecka Mendelssohn, which fits the greeting to his wife; Wilhelm Weber was unmarried and Gauss had died in 1855. Dedekind was close to both men.
- In summer 1857 Riemann was away from Göttingen recovering from overwork, at Bad Harzburg according to Dedekind's biographical sketch. The phrase 'bei meiner Rückkehr nach Göttingen' fits this.

The next page (folio 164v / 165) drafts a reply to someone who wished for more illustration by examples in the second part, and sketches definitions of simply and doubly connected surfaces. It belongs to the same correspondence about the Abelian functions paper.

results.what: Biographical and dating evidence: Riemann sent his memoir on Abelian functions to Borchardt (Crelle's Journal) on 2 July 1857 and offered a copy to his teacher, probably Dirichlet. Dedekind acted as intermediary in a request for Riemann's lecture announcement.
results.modern_name: Correspondence and dating of the submission of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (paper published 1857); biographical context from Dedekind's Lebenslauf

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a non-mathematical letter draft about a lecture announcement and the submission of the 1857 Abelian functions paper to Borchardt. Its only interest is the precise submission date and the social context. No mathematical content is present.
transcription_corrections: The place name read as 'Quickborn [?]' is very uncertain. Given that Riemann was recuperating in Bad Harzburg in summer 1857, a reading like 'Harzburg' should be considered.

The illegible deleted fragment in the second paragraph probably belongs to a first version of '... und werde bitte, Ihnen eine Abschrift davon bei meiner Rückkehr nach Göttingen vorlegen zu dürfen'. The later rewritten sentence reads approximately '..., nach Göttingen zurückkehren und dann um die Erlaubniß bitten, Ihnen eine Abschrift meiner Abhandlung vorlegen zu dürfen'.

The printed text at the bottom, upside down, is a 'Frachtkarte No. 2' form (von ... nach ..., abgegangen/angekommen den ... 185. um ... Uhr ...mittags; columns Aufgabe-No., Laufende No., Inhalt, Auslage, Porto, Franko). It is not part of Riemann's text.
'(164)' in the right margin is the archival folio number.
